claims.text: The initial feedstock is an unmodified FeCoNiCrAl high-entropy alloy with a particle size distribution of 15–45 μm.
Bond coats produced from the unmodified 15–45 μm FeCoNiCrAl feedstock fall short of the required thickness.
The proposed intervention is to apply a thin Hf coating to the FeCoNiCrAl feedstock particles before thermal spraying.
The Hf layer acts as a protective barrier during particle flight and impact.
The Hf layer delays the onset of feedstock oxidation during thermal spraying.
Reduced oxidation caused by the Hf layer enhances splat bonding.
The Hf-protected interface improves inter-splat cohesion.
Improved inter-splat cohesion increases coating build-up and deposition efficiency.
Hf-coated feedstock will produce a significantly thicker bond coat than unmodified 15–45 μm feedstock under identical spray conditions.
The thicker bond coat produced from Hf-coated feedstock will have comparable or improved coating integrity relative to the baseline.
The Hf-coated feedstock will maintain low as-sprayed oxidation relative to the baseline.
The intervention will remain effective under conventional thermal-spray conditions and typical elevated TBC service temperatures.
The benefit may be limited by nonuniform Hf coverage or substantial deviations from conventional spray parameters.
